sentences.text: Good morning.
How you doing?
Hey Alan, how you doing?
This meeting is being recorded.
I was just thinking before this call, I was thinking I could do it being introduced to some of your clients actually, you know, typical, typical Brit.
My teeth are just terrible.
What are you guys based out of Andy's?
Andy's just outside London.
I'm about an hour from Manchester.
Nice man.
Yeah, we don't have a.
Any clients overseas, but if I did, I would have recommended someone.
Yeah, we, we actually work mostly in the U.S.
probably about 95% of our clients are U.S.
based, so.
And pretty much all of our work is there.
We are based in HQ'd in, in London.
You ever over here?

I was living in LA in 23.

Well, 20 what we call 24°.
Yeah, boiling hot.
Yeah, 24 is good.
It is, it is.
Well, thank you for getting in touch with us and appreciate your time today.
So want to keep things as brief as possible.

These calls generally speaking are kind of, you know, just kind of get to know your business and what, what it is that you're trying to achieve and then we can obviously feedback what our, our solutions are and the best way that that we can help you.
So I appreciate your maybe considering selling your agency.
So yeah, we'd like be nice to hear more about your journey and how you got there, but I'll give you a little bit of background about us.
I don't know how much you know about Capital A Group, but we are Capital A, we're an M and A advisory.
We work exclusively in marketing services.
So we have the platform AgencyAgencies Code, which is our marketplace for agency owners to buy and sell.
We also have deal engines as well, which is a deal flow advisory.

And we work on the buy side as well as Capital A working for our clients who can either be agencies or sometimes they're private equity companies or they're private investors and they're looking to acquire marketing agencies.
So we work with those directly as well, helping them to acquire companies.
So the good thing is we get to see deals on both sides of the table.
We're not just here trying to sell into the industry, but actually part of the buy side as well.
Which is good.
That's good to know.
Yeah.
Be good to hear more about you Ardlan, and how you got your business started and what it is that you're.
Yeah, we, we technically started in 20 end of 2017 under this name.
It really took off in 2020.
And you know, we're dental specific and we're, you know, we do all pieces of marketing, not just media buying, so content creation, ad creatives, website SEO.
The bread and butter, you could say.
And we've, you know, we've grown to a significant amount, I would say where it's, I would say if, if there's an exit.
We've been approached by a couple guys to be honest.
One that I'm talking to for the past few months.
One that didn't go through because I mean we didn't like we just initially talked and we know we never went to the next step.
I think they didn't have.
They, they bought a few agencies and it seemed like they didn't have money at that point when it got to us.
And so they're like, well, let's talk end of the year.
But we're at like around 4 million EBITDA and.
Yeah.
So we just wanna see how that would work as far as selling it.
Brilliant.
Okay, well congratulations for getting offers.
That's the hard bit.
And what's the, the deal with the, the current conversation?
They're, they're not get, they're not getting to the difficult conversation and making you an.
What's the, the thing that's slowing that down?
So the guy owns a few companies.
He's not a typical PE guy and so he's.
The offer there is, this is verbally obviously but he's, he's seen all of our financials and everything and the offer is 30 and you know, just a matter of him.
But it's a deal structure that was taking a little bit long I guess according to him.
And obviously he's going to finance most of it.
So I think that's what he was going back and forth with.
So.
Yeah, I don't know what's taking him.
Private equity as well.
He's not a typical, like the, the first guy that didn't go anywhere who they were like private equity that were.
Their thesis was to buy dental specific and legal specific marketing companies.
Okay.
This guy's just an investor in lots of different types of businesses.
He's in dental.
He has different businesses that he thinks it could have synergy.
Yeah, that's.
Yeah.
Okay, cool.

So he's made, he's made a verbal offer or discussed what the size of the offer would look like because 7.5 is, is pretty good and it's kind of around what I would potentially expect would be sort of the low, lower to middle of, of what your range would be.
But what are you after, what's, what are you trying to achieve?
Because obviously you built something great.
It must be a tremendous cash machine to have $4 million being printed every year.
Yeah, I would like.
Yeah, I mean the deal structure is more important, honestly, like, so if they, if they hook me on for few years after, then it kind of beats the purpose.
But if it's like two years, I'm fine.
Yeah, that's the thing.
So.
Okay, so it's the, it's the earn out period that you're not looking forward to.
So just like, just as a very general rule of thumb, most agency deals, because they're service businesses, they do tend to have quite extended earnout periods.
So you know, some smaller businesses, three to six month handover period.
But agencies and service businesses in particular, they tend to have these two to five sometimes year earn outs attached to them.
And three years is very typical.

So the structure of a very typical deal would be, we agree, the valuation of the business, we give you 50% of the cash up front and then there's a three year period where you get the rest out in chunks.
So that's kind of very typical.
But I think given the size of the business, maybe we'll get into it how you've structured the business itself as well.
But given the size, I think there would be a lot of flexibility in the, the types of offers that we could get on the table.
How is the business owned?
Are you the 100% owner, founder, operator?
I have a partner.
You're a partner.
Okay.
And there are, there are a bunch of other equal partners or is it shareholders?
No, just am I.
Okay.
And, and in terms of your team, how, what's the size of your team?
Like 26 or seven people.
They're primarily, we have us based, but they're primarily outside of us.
All right, and the leadership, what does that look like?
Is there a layer of management?
There is one layer of management currently and then there's another one that's being added hopefully in the next two weeks.
Yeah.
So if you were to leave, would that, would that mean that the management team could just step in?
There would be no gaps in terms of delivery.
On the sales side, there will be no gaps on account management.
There would be no gaps because that's, we built that this past year.
But on the event side there will be gaps and that's why there's that person starting in two weeks.
Okay.
So we, we host events that basically that's how we get the leads.
And you know, I'm the one kind of coordinating that, so I get it.
Okay.
All right.
So you're kind of the face for those live events and, and you're bringing in some of the business.
Yes.
Okay.
And then what, what's, why, why the call today?
What, what's going on?
You're looking to exit the business?
Is there any issues or what, what's your reason?
You know, I, I talking to the first guys, I, when they approached me, I really didn't want to sell.
And so I didn't really like, put effort into it.
And I made, I would say, well, not without, they were not the right fit anyways.

But I learned that I, I'm not even prepared to, you know, have something presentable to show to them where, because I kind of noticed, like the way these guys work and, you know, they're asking questions, I'll respond to them, they want documents, I'll send it to them.
But I noticed that they're looking for a story, and that's what it seemed like on the back end.
So I was like, well, I need to, I need to pitch better if I needed, if I want to get a better offer.
So that's why I'm on this call.
Okay.
Yeah, that's definitely part of it.
I, I think, I think having a story, a cohesive story, and kind of already thinking through where you want to go is a good part of it.
But certainly the other thing is knowing what a good offer looks like and being able to leverage one against the other.
Right.
And the real value that we're bringing to the table is the process that we run.
So we're running roughly a sort of six month process.
And once we're up and running, we're set up, we're having you introduce, you know, probably two or three really good potential buyers each week.

And once we get to about two or three month point in that process, then we start to get maybe even earlier than that, but we start to push for offers from everybody you've spoken to that far, thus far.
And then the, the contention between those interested parties helps get us the best offers that are going to be because they understand other people are also bidden and they're in a process as well.
So, so that's the, the kind of beauty of what we're putting together, we're helping you really to achieve the, the best value for the business.
But also it gets you prepared, the process gets you prepared and also helps you understand what a good offer looks like.
I mean, at the moment I, I don't know how much experience you've got with M and A, but you may not even know whether seven and a half is good or whether you want a 10x or a 20x.
I mean, there's all sorts of stuff that appears in the press, so it's hard to know what a good offer can look like.
So yeah, we're bringing all of that process to the party as well.
Okay, so you're kind of, you're thinking now that you've had these few conversations that it is a good time to buy, sorry, sell the business.
Or, or are you just really thinking, let's see what it looks like, let's get a few offers in, we want to sell.
Yeah, I mean, again, if the offer is right, obviously.
Yeah, yeah, of course.
All right, so, so what we're doing is this, is this six month process.

So the, the way that we run this is, is quite a tight ship and it really suits founders like yourself who have decided that they want to sell because it kind of puts a limit on the length of time that we're in the market.
We don't want to be there too long.

And also, I mean, particularly now at this point in time, we've got a very sort of easy six month window where we can go to market, produce a ton of interest for the business, get some offers and get the deal closed before the end of the, the years.
There's a, there's a couple of quiet periods potentially sort of like August can be a really bad time when everybody's on holiday and certainly around December can be bad as well.
Sort of December, January can be bad as well.
So this, this period that we have now kind of flushes out those offers, particularly before Christmas.
When people see Christmas approaching as a deadline, you get those offers out and the deals can get closed really quickly.
So in terms of what, like what, what you're looking to do, obviously we're an M and A advisory.
Are you, are you looking to get the full process run on your behalf, like, you know, the valuation and all the marketing materials prepared?
You know, whereabouts are you in that whole process?
Yeah, we wouldn't approach, so we didn't really have anything prep, to be honest.
So it would make sense to do something like that.
Yeah.
Okay.
All right, so, so I think the, the Most suitable platform.
We offer a few different sort of flavors of what we do but the most suitable, the Platinum package.
And so basically this is a fully managed process.
Like I say it's a six month process, it's $25,000.
We can break that, that down, smaller payments if you need to.

But essentially what we're doing for that is we're getting you ready for market and that involves going through your financials, preparing evaluation and then what we call an im, some people call it a SIM or a cim which is like a pitch deck for bankers.
We're preparing all of that, the listings as well which go onto our platform agencies.
Co we put all of that prep work in that usually takes about two or three weeks to get up and running the setup and then we're marketing that out in a few different places.
So one of the key things is the agencies code platform.
We have a mailing list of about 20,000 agency owners and buyers on there.
So we get a lot of initial traction once we, we go live and we, we circulate that amongst our mailing list.
We actually had a, an agency in Los Angeles last year that did 45 signed NDAs in 24 hours.
So he had a really great choice of potential buyers.
I think he got five offers within a couple of months and it was one of the smoothest process we had had actually.
But agency.
How big was the size, the size of the deal?
How big was the deal on that one?
It was pretty small actually.
It was probably around the sort of million mark, something like that.
Pretty small.

One of the factors in that one was, was there was two factors I think one was it was quite small and the other one, one was because it was in la, so LA is one of the hotspots but we work on deals of all sorts of size, you know up to about 30, 40 million in deal value as well.
So yeah, so sorry, we're, we're putting together all of the marketing materials and we, we market to our, our market mailing list.
But also what we're doing is we're preparing a bespoke list of buyers as well.
So our analysts will go out into the marketplace.
We're going to basically you know, really drill down and find all of the potential buyers in the market.
So I would at a guess say the obvious places to look would be for private equity, particularly ones that are in dental already or any larger agencies or agency groups that are in dental.
And also outside of marketing as well, I'm sure there are some dental, dental groups that would be interested in this type of thing and bringing it in house.
So we would do all of that prep and build that bespoke list.
And that could be a list of maybe it could be somewhere between sort of 10 and 20,000, up to that many.
But we'll prepare that list, and then we're marketing the opportunity out to this cold list, our warm list, and any sort of direct buyers in our network as well, that we know personally.
And we handle all of those initial calls.
So we're pitching them, you know, we're pitching them the opportunity first, getting them warmed up for you, and then if they're a good fit and you.
You're happy to move forward with them, then we get you in a meeting with them, and that's really about a chemistry check.
If you like them, they like you, and then we can start to get the financials shared with them and get an offer.
And what we're doing is we're building this up with a bunch of different buyers and so that we have a deadline for offers.
And then that's the point when we want to get two or three offers on the table at least, and we can leverage those one against the other.
And then you kind of decide which is the best fit for you, and we can move forward with them.
So we take 5% on the deal and we net that off any fees that you pay.
So all the retainer fees is netted off to our win fees.
If it ends up being, say, 100k win fee, we take away the 25k that you paid.
Already got it.
Okay.
And then during this time, would we be exclusively listening with you, or let's say I have these side deals going on and let's say that goes through.
How would that work?
Yeah, so we do, we do prefer.
We do prefer exclusivity.

It makes it a lot easier for us to not compete against other M and A advisors, but also internally with you, because then there's a preference for one deal over the other, which doesn't always make it easy for either of us to get a deal close.
But that said, if you have deals or somebody's approach you directly and it's nothing to do with us, then the contract allows for that as well.
We have to actually generate the win fee ourselves.
If you find your own buyer, then of course you can get your deal closed completely separately.
And actually we have a, a tiered win fee as well, which is dependent on whether we find the buyer as well.
So if you wanted, for instance, if you said, look, Andy, I'VE got the buyer already, but I want you to negotiate on my behalf.
Then there's different tiers that we.
We have as well for that, so it kind of covers all scenarios.
Okay, perfect.
So what are you thinking?
What's the sort of.
Sort of position you're in at the moment?
Are you looking to pull the trigger today, in a few months or.
Whereabouts are you definitely this week?
I'm honestly doing a couple more calls and definitely want to pull the trigger this week.
Okay, cool.
All right.
How you fix for Friday morning?
Are you available at all?
Yeah, like, same time, actually, if that works for you.
Yeah.
Yeah, that's pretty cool.
Okay, let me put something in the.
The calendar and I'll.
I'll send you an invite after this call.
So what we'll do is we'll.
We'll put everything in an email so you've got it.
You've got our case studies as well, and that's a list of some of the people we work with, as well as, you know, feedback from.
From clients.
And.
And then we'll follow up on that call on Friday.
And if you are happy to go with us, we'll get the.
The whole onboarding process started and we'll.
We'll hit the ground running for June, hopefully, and we can be extremely quick in getting you set up and onboarded and listed and start getting some buyers in front of you.
Perfect.
Awesome, man.
Okay, thanks for your time.
Nice to meet you.
Likewise.
Take care.
Bye.
Bye.
Bye.
Bye.

summary.overview:
- Ardalan Safi's agency, founded in 2017, focuses on dental marketing with a $4M EBITDA and growing acquisition interest, indicating strong market positioning.
- Current verbal acquisition offer includes significant financing and an earn-out period, highlighting the need for clear deal structure understanding.
- Typical earn-out periods for agencies range from 2-5 years, with a standard of 3 years, emphasizing the importance of alignment on growth expectations.
- Agency has 26-27 employees, primarily international, with an impending management hire to enhance event coordination, indicating growth management strategies.
- Events are crucial for lead generation, currently managed by Ardalan, with plans for delegation to improve operational efficiency.
- Need for enhanced narrative and preparation to boost sale value recognized, driven by previous buyer interactions and industry insights.
- Capital A Group offers a structured six-month M&A process, focusing on tailored financial prep and marketing strategies to attract competitive offers.
- M&A process aims for pre-year-end market window, maximizing exposure through a bespoke buyer list and marketing channels.
- Fee structure for Capital A includes a $25,000 retainer and 5% success fee, offering flexibility in payment and exclusivity arrangements.
- Ardalan plans to select an advisor shortly, with a follow-up meeting scheduled to finalize decisions, indicating urgency in the M&A process.
summary.short_summary: Ardalan Safi's dental marketing agency, founded in 2017, is experiencing significant growth, reflected in its $4M EBITDA and increasing acquisition interest. Current acquisition offers involve considerable financing and an earn-out period typically set between 2-5 years, emphasizing the need for alignment on growth expectations. The agency employs 26-27 staff members, mainly international, and is poised for growth through a new management hire focused on event coordination. Events, crucial for lead generation, are currently managed by Ardalan, who plans to delegate responsibilities for improved efficiency. Recognition of the need for a compelling narrative and preparation to enhance sale value stems from past buyer interactions. Capital A Group is facilitating a structured six-month M&A process targeted before the year-end, with a fee structure of a $25,000 retainer and a 5% success fee, while Ardalan is set to choose an advisor soon to expedite the process.
